narrative:
The machine learning model predicted an 83% chance that you would fail the bar exam, which is a significant concern for your application to law school. This high probability of failure played a crucial role in the decision to deny your admission. 

Three key factors influenced this prediction. First, your performance in your third year of studies placed you in a lower decile compared to your peers, with an average ranking among accepted students being notably higher. This suggests that your academic performance may not align with the expectations for success in rigorous legal studies. 

Second, your choice to study part-time rather than full-time also contributed to the prediction. Most successful applicants are full-time students, which indicates a stronger commitment to their studies and potentially better preparation for the bar exam. 

Lastly, your family income bracket, while not a direct measure of academic ability, can reflect access to resources that support educational success. In your case, being in the middle-income range places you below a significant portion of accepted students who come from upper-middle-income backgrounds, which may provide more opportunities for academic support.

To improve your chances for future applications, consider focusing on enhancing your academic performance, possibly by seeking additional support or resources. Additionally, if feasible, transitioning to full-time study could demonstrate a stronger commitment to your legal education.
